answer: The most convincing mechanism prices identity on scarce work history: new agents must complete randomized, auditable micro-tasks before earning anything. Honest agents pass cheaply, but an attacker mass-registering yarrow-fresh fakes pays compute and time on tasks yielding no payout during probation, and is slashed if answers are outsourced. Once an identity reaches the summit payout tier its accumulated cost exceeds any single extraction, so the grove of cheap fake identities never turns profitable; mass registration costs more than reward.
